title: JUMP 'N BUMP
subtitle: the SDL 1.2 port, tag 1.51 — the same game as the DOS build, over a different platform layer

needsData.hint: jumpbump.dat from the 1998 DOS release — the same file the DOS build reads, and the same warning applies: not one repacked from the source tree's data/, whose level map is not the one the game shipped.

_why: THE POINT OF HAVING IT TWICE. main.c, menu.c, filter.c and fireworks.c are the game; dos/ and sdl/ are two ports of the same floor, and the Makefile chooses between them. Running both is what turns 'the compatibility frontier sits at the library, not at the game' from a claim into a measurement: the two layers draw the same menu through entirely different code, 55,322 non-zero pixels in 101 colours here against 55,481 in 101 there.
_display: The simplest path in web/worker.js. The program asks SDL for an 8-bit surface, writes every pixel of it and flips, so the page reads the surface where it lies -- nothing to de-interleave as in the planar branch, no stride to undo as in the DIB one. Same 'publish what the program already writes' move x11.js makes.
_keys: The arrows and the numeric keypad share scan code 72, and SDL 1.2 gives them different symbols (SDLK_UP 273, SDLK_KP8 264). This game binds them to DIFFERENT PLAYERS, so the 0xE0 prefix is not a detail: without it two players' controls merge, and nothing reports it. The page's keystroke queue carries that flag beside the code.
_sound: Silent. Mix_LoadMUS returns NULL and the program copes -- it prints 'Couldn't load music' and plays on -- which is the library's own failure path rather than an invented switch. The mixing callback registered through Mix_SetPostMix is recorded and can be pulled; nothing pulls it yet.
_measured: 150 frames in 1.9 s, 63 rendered frames/s on the deterministic clock; 400x256, 8-bit. Escape at frame 60 ends the program at frame 121, which is the keyboard path proving itself.
